analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page introduces three laws of motion, defines momentum and acceleration relations, explains inertia with net force, and illustrates action and reaction with flight examples.

overview.headline: Newton laws linking forces, mass and motion in straight line flight examples

keyPoints.point: Inertia keeps an object at rest or in motion at constant speed until an unbalanced force acts
keyPoints.quote: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

keyPoints.point: Acceleration from a force is proportional to force size and inversely proportional to object mass
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyPoints.point: Second law defines force as change in momentum which is mass times velocity per change in time
keyPoints.quote: His second law defines a force to be equal to change in momentum (mass times velocity) per change in time.

keyPoints.point: Every action has equal opposite reaction with forces resulting from interactions between objects
keyPoints.quote: His third law states that for every action (force) in nature there is an equal and opposite reaction.

keyTerms.gloss: tendency to resist changes in motion and remain at rest or uniform motion
keyTerms.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: mass times velocity used to define momentum and track motion change
keyTerms.quote: Momentum is defined to be the mass m of an object times its velocity V.

keyTerms.gloss: change in velocity divided by time that defines acceleration
keyTerms.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.

keyTerms.gloss: equal change in momentum caused over time by a push or pull
keyTerms.quote: His second law defines a force to be equal to change in momentum (mass times velocity) per change in time.

keyTerms.gloss: quantity with magnitude and direction associated with motion
keyTerms.quote: Scientists and mathematicians call this a vector quantity.
